pages.title: A Roadmap for a Greener Europe
pages.content:
Announced by the European Commission on 11 December 2019, the Green Deal serves as a growth strategy for sustainable development, which aims to protect the planet by creating a clean economy and reducing the EU’s net greenhouse gas emissions to zero by 2050. The Green Deal is the EU’s roadmap for making its economy, industry, and everyday life more environmentally friendly in order to tackle the climate crisis and ensure a healthier planet.

A major goal of this initiative is to use resources more efficiently by promoting the shift to a circular economy, focusing on recycling materials and reducing waste to protect nature. To reach this goal, it offers a master plan with practical policies and specific opportunities for this great transformation.

vocabulary.definition: Able to continue for a long time without harming the environment.
A gas, such as carbon dioxide, that traps heat in the air and makes the Earth warmer.
Gases that are sent into the air, for example by cars and factories.
An economy in which materials are reused, repaired, and recycled instead of being thrown away.

hotspots.title: A Growth Strategy
hotspots.description: Announced by the European Commission on 11 December 2019, the Green Deal serves as a growth strategy for sustainable development.

hotspots.title: Using Resources Efficiently
hotspots.description: A major goal of this initiative is to use resources more efficiently by promoting the shift to a circular economy.

exercises.title: Why a Roadmap?
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the chapter supports.
exercises.question: Why does the EU want to make its economy, industry and everyday life more environmentally friendly?
options: to tackle the climate crisis and ensure a healthier planet
to increase the use of fossil fuels
to reduce the number of member states
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “… more environmentally friendly in order to tackle the climate crisis and ensure a healthier planet.”

feedback.correct: Correct. To tackle the climate crisis.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the first paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: Announced By …
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose what the opening phrase does.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Announced by the European Commission on 11 December 2019, the Green Deal serves as a growth strategy …” What does “Announced by …” do?
options: It gives background information about the Green Deal in a short, formal way.
It tells us what the Green Deal will do next.
It is the main verb of the sentence.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A past participle clause at the start of a sentence (Announced by …) is a short, formal way to say “The Green Deal, which was announced by …”. The main verb is “serves”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Background information.
feedback.incorrect: Find the main verb of the sentence.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Formal Patterns
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 1.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: The Green Deal serves [choice] a growth strategy for sustainable development.
… which aims to protect the planet by [choice] a clean economy.
… more environmentally friendly in order [choice] the climate crisis.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Serve as” + role, “by + -ing” for method and “in order to + verb” for purpose.

feedback.correct: Well done. As, creating, to tackle.
feedback.incorrect: Check the word before each gap.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say it?

transformItems.source: Announced by the European Commission on 11 December 2019, the Green Deal serves as a growth strategy.
transformItems.frame: The Green Deal, [blank] was announced by the European Commission on 11 December 2019, serves as a growth strategy.

transformItems.source: A major goal of this initiative is to use resources more efficiently.
transformItems.frame: A major goal of this initiative is the more efficient [blank] of resources.

transformItems.source: It focuses on recycling materials and reducing waste to protect nature.
transformItems.frame: It focuses on recycling materials and reducing waste so [blank] nature is protected.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: A participle clause can become a relative clause. A verb (use) can become a noun (the use of). “To + verb” for purpose can become “so that”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Same meaning, new structure.
feedback.incorrect: Use which, use and that.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: A Roadmap for Our School
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write a formal paragraph of six to seven sentences presenting a green roadmap for your school.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the aim, and how will it be reached?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “Prepared by our class, this roadmap aims to make our school more sustainable. Its main goal is to use resources more efficiently. We will reduce paper waste by printing on both sides and sharing digital materials. We will also recycle plastic and glass in order to protect nature. Every class will choose an energy monitor. In this way, our school can become a model for the neighborhood.”

feedback.correct: Check: a participle clause, in order to and by + -ing.

discussionPrompts.question: Introduce the roadmap with a participle clause.
Give the aim with in order to.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What does the text call the Green Deal in the second sentence?
beforeYouRead.quote: The Green Deal is the EU’s roadmap

iCan: I can explain the Green Deal as a growth strategy and a roadmap.
I can explain how the shift to a circular economy protects nature.
I can use participle clauses and in order to in formal writing.

pages.title: The Key Priorities
pages.content:
The key priorities of the Green Deal are as follows:

Addressing Climate Change: The Green Deal emphasizes tackling climate change, which is one of the European Union’s top priorities. Within this framework, the EU and its member states aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 and achieve climate neutrality by 2050. This is a critical step toward limiting the effects of global warming and reducing the harmful impacts of climate change.

Sustainability: The Green Deal stresses the sustainable use of natural resources. It aims to prevent environmental problems such as deforestation, the depletion of water resources and the loss of biodiversity. The Green Deal also includes a commitment to protecting and restoring the environment, aiming to ensure clean air, clean water, healthy soil, and sustainable, healthy food for all.

Economic Transformation: The Green Deal aims to promote green technologies and environmentally friendly business models. In this way, it seeks to support economic growth in a sustainable manner.

vocabulary.definition: A state in which a country releases no more greenhouse gases than it removes from the air.
The cutting down of forests over a large area.
A fall in the amount of something until very little is left.
The variety of plants and animals that live in a place.

hotspots.title: A Critical Step
hotspots.description: This is a critical step toward limiting the effects of global warming and reducing the harmful impacts of climate change.

hotspots.title: Healthy Soil
hotspots.description: It aims to ensure clean air, clean water, healthy soil, and sustainable, healthy food for all.

exercises.title: Sustainability
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the chapter supports.
exercises.question: Which environmental problems does the Green Deal aim to prevent?
options: deforestation, the depletion of water resources and the loss of biodiversity
high prices and broken supply chains
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “It aims to prevent environmental problems such as deforestation, the depletion of water resources and the loss of biodiversity.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Deforestation, depletion and loss of biodiversity.
feedback.incorrect: Read the Sustainability paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: A Step Toward …-ing
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose the correct explanation.
languageFocusExercises.question: “This is a critical step toward limiting the effects of global warming …” Why is “limiting” an -ing form?
options: Because “toward” is a preposition, and a verb after a preposition takes -ing.
Because the action is happening now.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: After a preposition (toward, by, on, of), a verb takes the -ing form: a step toward limiting, a commitment to protecting.

feedback.correct: Correct. A preposition comes before it.
feedback.incorrect: What kind of word is “toward”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Preposition + -ing
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: This is a critical step toward [choice] the effects of global warming.
The Green Deal also includes a commitment to [choice] and restoring the environment.
The Green Deal emphasizes [choice] climate change.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Toward” and “to” (in “commitment to”) are prepositions, so they take -ing. “Emphasize” is followed by a noun or -ing.

feedback.correct: Well done. Limiting, protecting, tackling.
feedback.incorrect: Is there a preposition before the gap?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Verbs to Nouns
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence with a noun. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does formal writing use nouns?

transformItems.source: Water resources are depleted.
transformItems.frame: There is a [blank] of water resources.

transformItems.source: Biodiversity is lost.
transformItems.frame: There is a [blank] of biodiversity.

transformItems.source: The Green Deal commits to protecting the environment.
transformItems.frame: The Green Deal includes a [blank] to protecting the environment.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Formal texts often turn verbs into nouns: deplete → depletion, lose → loss, commit → commitment.

feedback.correct: Correct. Depletion, loss, commitment.
feedback.incorrect: Find the nouns in the Sustainability paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Our City’s Priorities
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write a formal paragraph of six to seven sentences on the three key environmental priorities of your city.
languageFocusExercises.question: What should your city focus on, and why?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “The key priorities of our city are as follows: clean air, water and green spaces. First, air pollution from traffic is a serious problem. More electric buses would be a critical step toward reducing it. Second, the depletion of our water resources is a growing risk. Third, the city should protect its parks and plant new trees. These steps would ensure a healthier life for all.”

feedback.correct: Check: as follows, a formal noun and step toward + -ing.

discussionPrompts.question: Introduce the priorities.
discussionPrompts.example: The key priorities of our city are as follows: …

discussionPrompts.question: Use a formal noun.
discussionPrompts.example: The depletion / loss / pollution of … is …

discussionPrompts.question: Use a step toward + -ing.
discussionPrompts.example: This is an important step toward …-ing …

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: By how much do the EU and its member states aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 2030?
beforeYouRead.quote: reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030

iCan: I can explain the three key priorities of the Green Deal.
I can explain the 2030 and 2050 targets and why they matter.
I can use step toward + -ing and formal nouns such as depletion and commitment.

pages.title: Why Is the Green Deal Essential?
pages.content:
The Green Deal is crucial because climate change and environmental degradation pose a severe risk to the planet. Traditional economic models that rely on heavy resource consumption and fossil fuels are no longer sustainable. Therefore, transitioning to a net-zero economy is seen as the key way to tackle the climate crisis, protect biodiversity, and ensure long-term energy security.

Indeed, energy security has become a critical challenge today as rising geopolitical tensions, global crises, and regional conflicts create constant uncertainty around the world. High energy prices and broken supply chains have seriously weakened the competitiveness of many companies, especially energy-intensive industries. These supply chains may face disruptions because ongoing conflicts threaten to block trade routes and stop the delivery of resources. As a result, electricity and fuel become scarce and expensive.

vocabulary.definition: Fuels such as coal, oil, and gas that formed underground from plants and animals millions of years ago.
Describes a balance in which the greenhouse gases we release are equal to the amount we remove from the air.
Changing from one system or situation to another.
Connected with how a country’s location and power affect its relations with other countries.

hotspots.title: No Longer Sustainable
hotspots.description: Traditional economic models that rely on heavy resource consumption and fossil fuels are no longer sustainable.

hotspots.title: Energy Security
hotspots.description: Indeed, energy security has become a critical challenge today.

exercises.title: Why Supply Chains Break
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the chapter supports.
exercises.question: Why may supply chains face disruptions?
options: because ongoing conflicts threaten to block trade routes and stop the delivery of resources
because renewable energy is too cheap
because companies use too little energy
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “These supply chains may face disruptions because ongoing conflicts threaten to block trade routes and stop the delivery of resources.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Conflicts threaten trade routes.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the second paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: Building an Argument
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose what “Therefore” and “Indeed” do.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Therefore, transitioning to a net-zero economy is seen as the key way …” “Indeed, energy security has become a critical challenge today …” What do the two linkers do?
options: “Therefore” gives a conclusion; “Indeed” adds strong support to the argument.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Therefore” introduces a logical conclusion. “Indeed” adds a point that makes the argument stronger.

feedback.correct: Correct. A conclusion, then support.
feedback.incorrect: Which one gives a result?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Formal Linkers
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does the writer connect the ideas?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Traditional economic models are no longer sustainable. [blank], transitioning to a net-zero economy is seen as the key way to tackle the climate crisis. [blank], energy security has become a critical challenge today. Conflicts threaten to block trade routes. [blank], electricity and fuel become scarce and expensive.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Therefore” and “As a result” introduce results. “Indeed” adds strong support.

feedback.correct: Well done. Therefore, Indeed, As a result.
feedback.incorrect: Is the next idea a result or extra support?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say it?

transformItems.source: Climate change and environmental degradation pose a severe risk to the planet.
transformItems.frame: Climate change and environmental degradation are a severe [blank] to the planet.

transformItems.source: Transitioning to a net-zero economy is seen as the key way to tackle the climate crisis.
transformItems.frame: Many people [blank] transitioning to a net-zero economy as the key way to tackle the climate crisis.

transformItems.source: Traditional economic models that rely on fossil fuels are no longer sustainable.
transformItems.frame: Traditional economic models that [blank] on fossil fuels are no longer sustainable.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Pose a risk” means “be a risk”. The passive “is seen as” becomes the active “people see … as”. “Rely on” means “depend on”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Same meaning, new structure.
feedback.incorrect: Use risk, see and depend.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: A Short Argument
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write an argument of six to seven sentences: Why should your country invest in energy security?
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the problem, and what follows from it?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “Energy security has become a critical challenge for many countries. Indeed, conflicts in other regions can raise energy prices at home. High prices weaken companies and make life harder for families. As a result, depending on imported fossil fuels is risky. Local renewable energy cannot be blocked by distant conflicts. Therefore, my country should invest more in wind and solar power. This would protect both the economy and the planet.”

feedback.correct: Check: a problem, indeed, as a result and therefore.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Which industries have high energy prices weakened most?

iCan: I can explain why the Green Deal is essential.
I can explain why energy security has become a critical challenge.
I can use formal linkers and the present perfect to build an argument.

pages.title: The Switch to Renewable Energy
pages.content:
To prevent these financial burdens, replace expensive fossil fuels, and end dependency on these traditional fuels, a growing number of countries are taking important steps to switch to renewable energy, such as wind and solar power, which is often cheaper. Sustaining industrial success in these uncertain times will require changing policies, moving toward renewable energy, and training workers with new skills.

This situation calls for a faster green transition to provide industries with affordable clean energy. Therefore, governments and organizations should design a comprehensive strategy based on a detailed analysis of investment needs for clean technology innovation and manufacturing.

vocabulary.definition: Energy from sources that do not run out, such as the wind and the sun.

hotspots.title: Wind and Solar Power
hotspots.description: A growing number of countries are taking important steps to switch to renewable energy, such as wind and solar power, which is often cheaper.

hotspots.title: A Comprehensive Strategy
hotspots.description: Governments and organizations should design a comprehensive strategy based on a detailed analysis of investment needs.

exercises.title: A Faster Transition
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the chapter supports.
exercises.question: Why does the situation call for a faster green transition?
options: to provide industries with affordable clean energy
to make fossil fuels more expensive for families
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “This situation calls for a faster green transition to provide industries with affordable clean energy.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Affordable clean energy for industries.
feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of the second paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: An -ing Subject
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose the subject.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Sustaining industrial success in these uncertain times will require changing policies …” What is the subject of “will require”?
options: Sustaining industrial success in these uncertain times
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A gerund phrase (Sustaining industrial success …) can be the subject of a sentence. It takes a singular verb.

feedback.correct: Correct. The whole -ing phrase is the subject.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: What will require something?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Verb Patterns
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: Sustaining industrial success will require [choice] policies.
This situation calls [choice] a faster green transition.
… to provide industries [choice] affordable clean energy.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Require + -ing”, “call for + noun” and “provide someone with something”.

feedback.correct: Well done. Changing, for, with.
feedback.incorrect: Which word goes with each verb?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say it?

transformItems.source: Countries want to end dependency on these traditional fuels.
transformItems.frame: Countries want to stop [blank] on these traditional fuels.

transformItems.source: … to provide industries with affordable clean energy.
transformItems.frame: … to provide affordable clean energy [blank] industries.

transformItems.source: A growing number of countries are taking important steps.
transformItems.frame: [blank] and more countries are taking important steps.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “End dependency on” becomes “stop depending on”. “Provide someone with something” becomes “provide something to / for someone”. “A growing number of” means “more and more”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Same meaning, new structure.
feedback.incorrect: Use depending, to and More.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: A Strategy Proposal
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write a formal proposal of six to seven sentences for a renewable energy strategy in your town.
languageFocusExercises.question: What does the town need, and why?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “Switching to renewable energy will require a clear plan and investment. Our town has many sunny days, so solar power is a sensible choice. Rising electricity bills call for quick action. Installing solar panels on public buildings would reduce costs. Training local workers would create new jobs. Therefore, the town council should design a strategy based on a detailed analysis of costs and benefits.”

feedback.correct: Check: a gerund subject, call for and should.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What does sustaining industrial success in uncertain times require?
options: changing policies, moving toward renewable energy, and training workers
beforeYouRead.quote: will require changing policies, moving toward renewable energy, and training workers with new skills.

iCan: I can explain why countries are switching to renewable energy.
I can explain what industrial success requires.
I can use gerund subjects and require / call for + noun.

pages.title: The Birth of a Net-Zero Era
pages.content:
The coming decades are likely to see the birth of a net-zero era, a period when the greenhouse gases we release are balanced by the amount we remove from the air. This new economic structure brings with it fresh markets, advanced clean technologies, and a complete transformation of our existing energy systems. Consequently, countries that choose to invest first and move faster today can secure a strong place in this emerging economy. These nations can also become global leaders both in clean technology and in addressing climate change and environmental pollution.

The transition to a green economy naturally leads to the creation of new industries requiring newly skilled workers while modernizing factories for eco-friendly production. To support this, the EU introduced the Net-Zero Industry Act to help build key green technologies such as batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, solar panels, and systems that capture and store carbon dioxide.

vocabulary.definition: Not harmful to the environment.

hotspots.title: A Net-Zero Era
hotspots.description: The coming decades are likely to see the birth of a net-zero era.

hotspots.title: The Net-Zero Industry Act
hotspots.description: To support this, the EU introduced the Net-Zero Industry Act to help build key green technologies.

exercises.title: Who Can Lead?
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the chapter supports.
exercises.question: Which countries can secure a strong place in the emerging economy?
options: countries that choose to invest first and move faster today
countries with the largest oil reserves
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “Consequently, countries that choose to invest first and move faster today can secure a strong place in this emerging economy.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Early investors who move fast.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of the first paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: Are Likely To
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose how certain the writer is.
languageFocusExercises.question: “The coming decades are likely to see the birth of a net-zero era …” How certain is the writer?
options: fairly certain, but not completely sure
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Be likely to + verb” shows that something will probably happen. It is less certain than “will”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Probable, not certain.
feedback.incorrect: Compare “are likely to see” with “will see”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Forms from the Chapter
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 5.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: The coming decades are likely [choice] the birth of a net-zero era.
This new economic structure brings [choice] it fresh markets.
These nations can become global leaders both in clean technology [choice] in addressing climate change.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Be likely to + verb”, “bring with it” and “both … and”.

feedback.correct: Well done. To see, with, and.
feedback.incorrect: Check the word before and after each gap.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say it?

transformItems.source: The coming decades are likely to see the birth of a net-zero era.
transformItems.frame: A net-zero era will [blank] begin in the coming decades.

transformItems.source: The transition naturally leads to the creation of new industries.
transformItems.frame: The transition naturally [blank] new industries.

transformItems.source: Consequently, early investors can secure a strong place.
transformItems.frame: As a [blank], early investors can secure a strong place.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Be likely to” becomes “will probably”. “Lead to the creation of” becomes “create”. “Consequently” means “as a result”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Same meaning, new structure.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: A Forecast
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write a forecast of six to seven sentences about your country’s economy in a net-zero era.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is likely to change, and what will follow?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “The coming decades are likely to bring big changes to our economy. Solar and wind energy are likely to become our main sources of electricity. Consequently, new factories will need workers who can build and repair green technology. Both universities and vocational schools will have to train these workers. Some old jobs are likely to disappear. However, countries that prepare early can become leaders. My country should invest now.”

feedback.correct: Check: likely to, consequently and both … and.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What are the coming decades likely to see?
options: the birth of a net-zero era
beforeYouRead.quote: The coming decades are likely to see the birth of a net-zero era

iCan: I can explain what the net-zero era will bring.
I can explain which countries can become global leaders.
I can use likely to, consequently and both … and.

pages.title: New Rules for Greener Products
pages.content: New rules for eco-friendly products and clean energy sources are important for the shift to a sustainable economy. These rules help create strong and successful systems for building, reusing, and recycling green technologies around the world. Specific examples of these rules include strict bans on destroying unsold clothing, as well as requirements to make spare parts easily accessible for repairs. In the future, modern regulations will apply to a much broader range of everyday products. This means factories will need to follow strict sustainability standards to protect nature. Governments will give top priority to developing net-zero technologies under these new eco-friendly plans.

hotspots.title: Strict Bans
hotspots.description: Specific examples of these rules include strict bans on destroying unsold clothing.

hotspots.title: Accessible Spare Parts
hotspots.description: The rules also include requirements to make spare parts easily accessible for repairs.

exercises.title: What the Rules Mean
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the chapter supports.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “This means factories will need to follow strict sustainability standards to protect nature.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the chapter.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: A Ban On …-ing
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose the correct explanation.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Specific examples of these rules include strict bans on destroying unsold clothing, as well as requirements to make spare parts easily accessible …” Which forms follow “ban” and “requirement”?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Some nouns have fixed patterns: a ban on + -ing (or noun), a requirement to + verb.

feedback.correct: Correct. Ban on + -ing, requirement to + verb.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Noun Patterns
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 6.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: These rules include strict bans on [choice] unsold clothing.
… requirements [choice] spare parts easily accessible for repairs.
Modern regulations will apply [choice] a much broader range of everyday products.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Ban on + -ing”, “requirement to + verb” and “apply to”.

feedback.correct: Well done. Destroying, to make, to.
feedback.incorrect: Which preposition or form goes with each noun or verb?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say it?

transformItems.source: There are strict bans on destroying unsold clothing.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Draft a Regulation
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write a short regulation of six to seven sentences for products sold at your school.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is banned, and what is required?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “From next term, there will be a ban on selling drinks in single-use plastic bottles at our school. The canteen will have a requirement to offer drinks in glass or refillable bottles. There will also be a requirement to label food that contains a lot of sugar. These rules apply to the canteen and to all school events. Students who bring their own bottle will get a small discount. The aim is to reduce waste and protect our health. These rules will be reviewed at the end of the year.”

feedback.correct: Check: ban on, requirement to and apply to.

discussionPrompts.question: Introduce a ban.
discussionPrompts.example: There will be a ban on …-ing …

discussionPrompts.question: Introduce a requirement.

pages.title: Everyday Choices and the Future of Work
pages.content:
In fact, the success of the Green Deal depends heavily on consumers making smart, eco-friendly choices driven by transparent information. People should easily see how sustainable, durable, and clean a product is before they buy it. Clear and accessible data helps individuals choose green products instead of traditional, high-emission options. For instance, energy labels on household appliances allow users to compare different choices effortlessly. Providing consumers with more information is a major step toward a successful green transition.

This economic transformation is also reshaping the labor market. As part of this change, the number of green jobs has been increasing rapidly in recent years. This shift is creating a huge demand for new skills at all levels, requiring large-scale training programs to help workers learn new technologies. Clean energy and eco-friendly manufacturing industries continue to need additional personnel. As a result, there will be strong competition for specialized talent in the near future.

pages.title: Education and Our Shared Future
pages.content:
In conclusion, the success of the green transition will depend largely on how well nations can train workers and educate society. This is true for industrial productivity based on innovation and resource efficiency, for a fair transition that prevents social injustice, and for reaching net-zero goals. Because of this, a major part of the Green Deal focuses on education. It helps all people learn essential green and digital skills. Fostering an informed and aware society through education and workforce training is essential for the world’s shared future.

Leaders, organizations, and citizens should all support these steps to turn these ideas into concrete actions for a cleaner world. In an interconnected world where the green transition extends across all borders, it is helpful for nations to keep working closely with their international partners. Türkiye also published its own Green Deal Action Plan in 2021 and set a goal of reaching net-zero emissions by 2053.

exercises.title: Notice: How Certain Is the Writer?
exercises.instructions: Sort the sentences by how certain the writer is.
exercises.question: Is the writer sure, or is it a probability?

items: The European Commission announced the Green Deal on 11 December 2019.
The EU introduced the Net-Zero Industry Act.
Türkiye published its own Green Deal Action Plan in 2021.
The coming decades are likely to see the birth of a net-zero era.
These supply chains may face disruptions.
These nations can also become global leaders.

Fact or certainty: The European Commission announced the Green Deal on 11 December 2019.
The EU introduced the Net-Zero Industry Act.
Türkiye published its own Green Deal Action Plan in 2021.
Probability or possibility: The coming decades are likely to see the birth of a net-zero era.
These supply chains may face disruptions.
These nations can also become global leaders.

exercises.explanation: Past facts use the past simple. “Are likely to”, “may” and “can” show probability or possibility.

Announcing in 2019, the Green Deal serves as a growth strategy.
Announced in 2019, the European Commission serves the Green Deal.
exercises.explanation: A past participle clause has a passive meaning, and its subject must be the subject of the main clause: the Green Deal was announced.

feedback.correct: Correct. The Green Deal was announced.
feedback.incorrect: Who or what was announced?

feedback.incorrect: Read the words around each gap.

exercises.title: Use: Check a Short Text
exercises.instructions: A student wrote a paragraph about energy. Find each mistake.
exercises.question: What should the student change?

errorItems.sentence: Switch to renewable energy will require investment.
Energy prices has been rising for years.
There is a commitment to reduce waste at our school.

exercises.explanation: Use a gerund as a subject, “have” with a plural subject, and -ing after the preposition “to” in “commitment to”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Switching, have been rising, commitment to reducing.
feedback.incorrect: Check the subject and the form after “to”.

exercises.title: Use: A Policy Brief
exercises.instructions: Write eight to ten sentences: Which part of the Green Deal matters most for your country?
exercises.question: Which part, why, and what is a counterpoint?
exercises.explanation: Example: “In my view, the switch to renewable energy matters most for my country. Indeed, energy security has become a critical challenge, and fuel prices depend on distant conflicts. Switching to wind and solar power would reduce this dependency. Moreover, it would create new green jobs. However, some people argue that education matters more, because new industries need newly skilled workers. This is a fair point. Without trained workers, new technologies cannot succeed. In conclusion, renewable energy and education must go together.”

feedback.correct: Check: a position, evidence, a counterpoint and in conclusion.

discussionPrompts.question: State your position with evidence.
discussionPrompts.example: In my view, … matters most because …

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole book together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: The Roadmap
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: What does the EU want to make more environmentally friendly with its roadmap?
options: its economy, industry, and everyday life
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “The Green Deal is the EU’s roadmap for making its economy, industry, and everyday life more environmentally friendly …”

feedback.correct: Correct. Economy, industry and everyday life.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second sentence of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Terms and Meanings
exercises.instructions: Match each term with its meaning.
exercises.question: What do the terms mean?

matchingPairs.right: a fall until very little is left
about location, power and relations between countries
the cutting down of forests over a large area
changing from one system to another

correctAnswer.depletion: a fall until very little is left
correctAnswer.geopolitical: about location, power and relations between countries
correctAnswer.deforestation: the cutting down of forests over a large area
correctAnswer.transitioning: changing from one system to another

exercises.explanation: These terms appear in Chapters 2 and 3.

feedback.correct: Correct. Each term matches its meaning.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the Word Notes.

exercises.title: The Target
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 2 with one number.
exercises.question: By how much does the EU aim to reduce emissions by 2030?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The EU and its member states aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least [blank]% by 2030.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “… reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 …”

feedback.correct: Correct. 55.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first priority in Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Uncertainty
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: What creates constant uncertainty around the world?
options: rising geopolitical tensions, global crises, and regional conflicts
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “… rising geopolitical tensions, global crises, and regional conflicts create constant uncertainty around the world.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Tensions, crises and conflicts.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Causes and Results
exercises.instructions: Match each cause with its result.
exercises.question: What follows?

matchingPairs.left: Conflicts threaten to block trade routes.
matchingPairs.right: Electricity and fuel become scarce and expensive.

matchingPairs.left: Countries invest first and move faster.
matchingPairs.right: They can secure a strong place in the new economy.
There will be strong competition for specialized talent.

matchingPairs.left: The transition extends across all borders.
matchingPairs.right: Nations should keep working with international partners.

correctAnswer.Conflicts threaten to block trade routes: Electricity and fuel become scarce and expensive.
They can secure a strong place in the new economy.
There will be strong competition for specialized talent.
correctAnswer.The transition extends across all border: Nations should keep working with international partners.

exercises.explanation: These causes and results appear in Chapters 3, 5, 7 and 8.

feedback.correct: Correct. Each cause matches its result.
feedback.incorrect: Look for as a result and consequently.

exercises.title: Broader Rules
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: The book says the regulations will apply to fewer products in the future.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “In the future, modern regulations will apply to a much broader range of everyday products.”

feedback.correct: Correct. A much broader range.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 6.

exercises.title: Consumers
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: The success of the Green Deal depends heavily on consumers making smart, eco-friendly choices.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “In fact, the success of the Green Deal depends heavily on consumers making smart, eco-friendly choices driven by transparent information.”

feedback.correct: Correct. It depends heavily on consumers.
feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: Skills
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 8 with one word.
exercises.question: What does education help all people learn?
exercises.fillBlanksText: It helps all people learn essential green and [blank] skills.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8: “It helps all people learn essential green and digital skills.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Digital.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 8.

exercises.title: Requirements
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: What will sustaining industrial success in uncertain times require?
options: changing policies, moving toward renewable energy, and training workers with new skills
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “Sustaining industrial success in these uncertain times will require changing policies, moving toward renewable energy, and training workers with new skills.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Policies, renewable energy and training.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the first paragraph of Chapter 4.

exercises.title: Put the Dates in Order
exercises.instructions: Put the events in order.
exercises.question: What comes first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: The European Commission announces the Green Deal (2019).
Türkiye publishes its Green Deal Action Plan (2021).
The EU aims for emissions at least 55% lower (2030).
The EU aims to achieve climate neutrality (2050).
Türkiye aims to reach net-zero emissions (2053).

exercises.explanation: The dates come from Chapters 1, 2 and 8.

feedback.correct: Correct. From 2019 to 2053.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the years.
